trickyParts: The registry heartbeat runs on a one-connection pool of its own: on the shared pool it broke cmd/dispatch's silent-database shutdown check (waitUntilIdle reads a handed-back connection as a database still answering).
/healthz fleet_commit is the announcer's cached read of the latest announcement (no statement per probe): null before the announcer's first pass, up to one 5 s pass behind the table.

The bus option WithConnectInBackground uses nats.go RetryOnFailedConnect so only nats.go dials before the first connection; the owning client reconciles the stream as its first reconnect hook. WithSilentCutDetection pings every 1 s with 2 outstanding.

Refresh classification: only 400/401 invalid_grant (and the rule checks) end a sign-in; every other refresh failure returns ErrIssuerUnavailable, answered 503 SIGNIN_UNAVAILABLE with the sign-in kept.

Envoy-dispatch accepts DISPATCH_SIGNIN_DOMAIN only with Google's issuer, so local and test sign-ins run in group mode; dev-oidc-issuer --sign-in-group makes the default person carry the Cognito pool claims.
A registry heartbeat that lapsed checks keys again; a live one only stamps. Both take the registry advisory lock, so the decision is ordered against Register.
